key_insight: Zero-shot compositional action recognition models mainly fail because they take object-driven 'verb shortcuts'—relying on object cues to predict verbs—rather than learning true verb semantics. Fixing this requires addressing sparse/skewed compositional supervision and asymmetric learning between verbs and objects.
problem_solved: Reduces object-driven shortcut behavior in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition (ZS-CAR), improving generalization to unseen verb–object combinations by forcing models to learn verbs more robustly instead of overfitting to object cues.
method: Systematic diagnosis: quantify shortcut behavior and trace it to two factors—extreme sparsity/skewness in compositional labels and asymmetric learning difficulty between verbs and objects.

Targeted mitigations: introduce compositional reweighting and verb-focused training (e.g., object masking/augmentation, disentangled/contrastive objectives) to suppress object shortcuts and amplify verb signals.
Evaluation: validate interventions on standard ZS-CAR benchmarks, measuring improved accuracy on held-out verb–object combos and reduced object-driven confusions.
impact: Provides practitioners with principled diagnostics and lightweight fixes to make action recognition models truly compositional and more reliable in zero-shot settings—critical for deploying models that must generalize to novel interactions.
visual_elements: Schematic illustrating an object-driven shortcut: object icon → wrong verb prediction vs. desired verb-focused pathway
Heatmap or bar chart showing compositional supervision sparsity/skewness across verb–object pairs
Before/after confusion matrices or accuracy bars comparing baseline vs. mitigated model on unseen compositions
Pipeline diagram of mitigation techniques (masking/augmentation, reweighting, contrastive/disentanglement) with arrows to improved generalization
paper_title: Why Can't I Open My Drawer? Mitigating Object-Driven Shortcuts in Zero-Shot Compositional Action Recognition
paper_authors: Geo Ahn, Inwoong Lee, Taeoh Kim, Minho Shim, Dongyoon Wee
